domestic.debt_note: July 2026 government domestic debt and liabilities were reported at Rs59.41 trillion, up 7.61% YoY and down 0.28% MoM; FY26 fiscal deficit was 2.6% of GDP with a 2.9% primary surplus.
domestic.remittances: August 2026 workers' remittances were $3.656 billion versus $3.630 billion in July; inflows remain an external-account cushion.
domestic.current_account: July 2026 current-account deficit was $328 million; August 2026 balance-of-payments data was not yet available at this checkpoint.

global_read: Global tape remains risk-off for PSX: Brent $108.97 (+4.17% 1d, +23.1% 1mo), WTI $104.24 (+4.19% 1d, +26.5% 1mo), VIX 17.75 (+12.06% 1d), USD/PKR +2.98% 1d, while S&P 500 and Dow remain negative over one month.
drivers: SBP's September 14, 2026 Monetary Policy Statement confirmed an 11.5% policy-rate hold by a 7-of-10 majority. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/assets/document/publications/MPS-Sep-2026-Eng.pdf
SBP's monetary-policy calendar lists September 14, 2026 as the latest MPC date and October 26, 2026 as the next scheduled MPC meeting. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/our-operations/monetary-policy

PBS reported August 2026 CPI at 11.1% YoY versus 9.2% in July; urban and rural core inflation were 8.8% and 8.5%, respectively. Source: https://www.pbs.gov.pk/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Monthly-Review-August-2026.pdf
SBP's September 14 statement reported FX reserves at $21.4 billion after Eurobond proceeds and continued FX purchases. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/assets/document/publications/MPS-Sep-2026-Eng.pdf

SBP EasyData recorded workers' remittances of $3,656.33767 million in August 2026 and $3,630.476883 million in July 2026. Source: https://easydata.sbp.org.pk/apex/f?cs=1B95E07DAC54300CB4A05B1C40048156D&p=10%3A220%3A7403577288980%3A%3ANO%3ARP%3AP220_SERIES_KEY%2CP220_PAGE_ID%3ATS_GP_BOP_WR_M.WR0340%2C1

The Finance Division reported a July 2026 current-account deficit of $328 million, with goods-and-services imports exceeding exports but remittances and services partly offsetting the gap. Source: https://www.finance.gov.pk/economic/Monthly_Economic_Update_and_Outlook_August_2026.pdf
SBP's latest displayed auction cutoffs were 11.899% for the 6-month MTB and 12.300% for the 10-year fixed PIB. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/bsd/2006/CL4.htm

A September 2026 report citing SBP data put July government domestic debt and liabilities at Rs59.41 trillion, up 7.61% YoY and down 0.28% MoM. Source: https://mettisglobal.news/Govt-domestic-debt-liabilities-rise-8-YoY-in-July-63255
The Finance Division reported FY26 fiscal deficit at 2.6% of GDP and primary surplus at 2.9% of GDP. Source: https://www.finance.gov.pk/economic/Monthly_Economic_Update_and_Outlook_August_2026.pdf

The IMF completed Pakistan's third EFF review and second RSF review on May 8, 2026, releasing about $1.1 billion under the EFF and $220 million under the RSF; the fourth EFF review was scheduled for September 15, 2026. Sources: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf and https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/cr/2026/english/1pakea2026001.pdf
SBP's data calendar places the August 2026 balance-of-payments summary in the September 16 release window. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/data-calendar

next_events.event: SBP analyst briefing for the September 14 MPC; IMF fourth EFF review availability window.
Scheduled SBP release window for August 2026 balance-of-payments data.
